title: How customers find their way around
summary: Your shop floor is something the game has to navigate: Supermarket Simulator gives customers a queue and a waypoint path, and it manages the entrance they come in through.
body: Customers are not placed in front of a shelf: they follow a path set out in the game, which is why a clear route through the shop matters.
Waiting is modelled as a queue, so the till area is a place where customers gather rather than stand in a line you drew.
The entrance is managed by the game and can change over time, which is why a shop can be reorganised without breaking the way people come in.
What this entry does not tell you: how many customers fit, how long they wait or how far they will walk. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Customers follow a path laid out by the game.
Waiting at the till is handled as a queue.
The shop entrance is managed and can change.
The shop defines dedicated restock areas, on foot and for vehicles.
The game builds a navigation mesh of its own, with a registry, a loader and a source object for it.
Paths can leave the mesh, and the links that join them have a navigator of their own.
The store entrance is built from named pieces: brick, wall and trim, each with a colour sheet of its own.
The entrance pieces also carry normal maps and a metallic-smoothness sheet.
facts.evidence: asset names: T_StoreEntrance_Trim_Normal, T_StoreEntrance_Brick_Normal, T_StoreEntrance_Wall_Normal, T_StoreEntrance_Trim_MetallicSmoothness
